classification.difficultyReason: Requires relating a sector arc to cone circumference, finding perpendicular height and calculating exact volume.

content.prompt: The two straight edges of each of the circular sectors below are joined to form a cone. Find the volume of each resulting cone.

spec.description: Unfilled 45-degree sector with horizontal lower radius and upper radius rising to the right.
spec.mathematics: Sector radius 8 cm; central angle 45 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied radius and angle are visible.

inlines.text: The arc becomes the circumference; use Pythagoras to find the height.

answer.worked:
The sector radius is the cone's slant length. Its arc becomes the cone's circumference.
$$\begin{align*}L&=\frac{45}{360}\times2\pi\times8\\L&=2\pi\ \mathrm{cm}\\2\pi r&=2\pi\\r&=1\ \mathrm{cm}\\h&=\sqrt{8^2-1^2}\\h&=3\sqrt7\ \mathrm{cm}\\V&=\frac13\pi r^2h\\V&=\frac13\pi(1)^2(3\sqrt7)\\V&=\pi\sqrt7\ \mathrm{cm}^3\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Unfilled 60-degree sector with horizontal lower radius and upper radius rising to the right.
spec.mathematics: Sector radius 12 cm; central angle 60 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied radius and angle are visible.

inlines.text: The arc becomes the circumference; use Pythagoras to find the height.

answer.worked:
The sector radius is the cone's slant length. Its arc becomes the cone's circumference.
$$\begin{align*}L&=\frac{60}{360}\times2\pi\times12\\L&=4\pi\ \mathrm{cm}\\2\pi r&=4\pi\\r&=2\ \mathrm{cm}\\h&=\sqrt{12^2-2^2}\\h&=2\sqrt{35}\ \mathrm{cm}\\V&=\frac13\pi r^2h\\V&=\frac13\pi(2)^2(2\sqrt{35})\\V&=\frac{8\pi\sqrt{35}}3\ \mathrm{cm}^3\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
The sector radius is the cone's slant length. Its arc becomes the cone's circumference.
$$\begin{align*}L&=\frac{90}{360}\times2\pi\times8\\L&=4\pi\ \mathrm{cm}\\2\pi r&=4\pi\\r&=2\ \mathrm{cm}\\h&=\sqrt{8^2-2^2}\\h&=2\sqrt{15}\ \mathrm{cm}\\V&=\frac13\pi r^2h\\V&=\frac13\pi(2)^2(2\sqrt{15})\\V&=\frac{8\pi\sqrt{15}}3\ \mathrm{cm}^3\end{align*}$$

spec.mathematics: Sector radius 12 cm; central angle 120 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied radius and angle are visible.

inlines.text: The arc becomes the circumference; use Pythagoras to find the height.

answer.worked:
The sector radius is the cone's slant length. Its arc becomes the cone's circumference.
$$\begin{align*}L&=\frac{120}{360}\times2\pi\times12\\L&=8\pi\ \mathrm{cm}\\2\pi r&=8\pi\\r&=4\ \mathrm{cm}\\h&=\sqrt{12^2-4^2}\\h&=8\sqrt2\ \mathrm{cm}\\V&=\frac13\pi r^2h\\V&=\frac13\pi(4)^2(8\sqrt2)\\V&=\frac{128\pi\sqrt2}3\ \mathrm{cm}^3\end{align*}$$
